name: Funk B
summary: Rare, 1930s-designed two-seat strut-braced high-wing cabin monoplane from Akron, Ohio and later Kansas, with fabric-covered wooden wings and a steel-tube fuselage.

engines: Single small flat-four in a smooth cowl
tail: Conventional fin and rudder with a horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Small strut-braced high-wing two-seater on a tailwheel
Fabric fuselage with a smoothly cowled engine

confusedWith.howToTell: Both are small fabric two-seat taildraggers; the Funk is far rarer, so check the cabin and cowl shape against Taylorcraft photos.
Both are side-by-side fabric taildraggers; the Funk is much rarer, with a more streamlined cabin and smoother cowl.
The Funk is fabric-covered; the Luscombe is all-metal with a polished skin.
